summary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX. The subject is unmoved at d37eb536... mode 0444, and every one of its cited digests reproduces against live bytes, including v2, both Stage A verdicts, frozen v1, COORD, file 08 and HEAD. Both occupancy verdicts are 0444 and both are ACCEPT 0/0. The draft opens no Class A, pins no QUALIFIED, SATISFIES nothing, records no row SATISFIED, does not record frozen v1 as a current remasurement, does not close leftover-design of OBL-G20-FX-AUTHORING, does not steal OBL-SDK-API-RESERVED, does not edit file 08, adds no DR-G* row, leaves live required-now at 28, names all fifty of D-167 through D-216 including D-168, does not authorize docs/v2/implementation/, and correctly declines to claim that D-056 gates 2 and 3 do not hold. The single SHOULD-FIX is an honesty-work omission: Codex Stage A carries two labeled observations, G20V2-OBS-01 and G20V2-OBS-02, and the draft's paragraph 4 drops both identifiers while preserving all three Claude identifiers. D-215 — the same class of entry, the same reviewer, the same verdict schema and the same paragraph slot — named all three of its Codex observation identifiers, and D-216 disclosed Claude's observations even though they were unlabeled. The asymmetry is not a false statement, but it silently loses two identifiers the series otherwise preserves.

shouldFix.title: Codex Stage A honesty observations G20V2-OBS-01 and G20V2-OBS-02 do not travel
shouldFix.where: Decision paragraph 4, draft lines 119-123 — the sentence 'Codex Stage A returned zero advisories.'
shouldFix.claimUnderTest: That paragraph 4 records the honesty work returned by both Stage A reviewers.
shouldFix.measurement: harness.DR-G20.component-operability.v2.review-independent.codex.json carries advisoryCount 0 but observationCount 2, in the key observationsNotFindings, with labeled identifiers G20V2-OBS-01 (the g20-input-corpus.v1 NAMES-only one-placeholder shape) and G20V2-OBS-02 (bare NT numbers against two live NT sequences). Neither identifier, and no mention of the observations at all, appears anywhere in the draft.
shouldFix.whyThisIsAFinding: The series preserves reviewer honesty identifiers, and does so specifically for this reviewer and this key. D-215 — same class of entry, same reviewer, same verdict schema, same paragraph-4 slot, two entries back — wrote 'Codex Stage A returned zero advisories and three honesty observations, not findings: G16V5-OBS-1 ..., G16V5-OBS-2 ..., and G16V5-OBS-3 ...', naming all three. Its Codex verdict had the identical shape: advisoryCount 0, observationCount 3, key observationsNotFindings. D-216 is not a counterexample: Claude's observations there carried no identifiers, and the draft still disclosed them as 'three unlabeled observations'. So the practice is that observations are disclosed, and that labeled ones travel by identifier. D-217 does neither. The standing obligation is on the record too: OBL-ADVISORY-HONESTY in sdk-leftover-join.v5 — the current DR-125 leftover-join this very draft cites — reasons that reviewer observations 'travel as honesty work' and that a join 'does not discharge them'. Dropping two labeled ones at the recording step is precisely the discharge that obligation forbids. The asymmetry is sharpest inside the paragraph itself: it preserves three Claude identifiers and says of them 'Those Claude identifiers travel as honesty work', then applies no such rule to the Codex side.
shouldFix.notAMustFixBecause: No statement in the draft is false. 'Codex Stage A returned zero advisories' is literally correct against advisoryCount 0, and Codex itself labels the two items observationsNotFindings with whyNotFinding rationales. No scope, authority, gate, count or SATISFIED effect turns on it, and both identifiers survive in the 0444 Stage A verdict. The defect is that the COORD record — the durable artifact — loses them.
shouldFix.remedy: Extend the paragraph-4 Codex sentence on the D-215 pattern, for example: 'Codex Stage A returned zero advisories and two honesty observations, not findings: G20V2-OBS-01 (g20-input-corpus.v1 uses the NAMES-only one-placeholder shape) and G20V2-OBS-02 (bare NT numbers against two live NT sequences). Those identifiers travel as honesty work.' Note that G20V2-OBS-02 is one shared class with CLAUDE-G20-V2-A1, which raises the same bare-NT ambiguity; if the successor records that sharing, both identifiers should still be preserved, as D-215 did for its own shared class G16V5-OBS-2.

observationsNotFindings.observation: The draft does not characterize frozen v1's verdict grade, where D-216 characterized each of its frozen predecessors ('Claude-REJECT occupancy', 'dual-REJECT occupancy').
observationsNotFindings.whyNotFinding: G20 v1 was Claude ACCEPT 0/0 with Codex not reviewed, so there is no adverse standing that silence could hide, and D-216's characterizations existed because its predecessors carried REJECTs that a reader must not mistake for acceptances. The draft makes no claim that v1 was dual-reviewed, scopes its Stage A table to v2, and states the operative protection twice — v1 stays frozen and is not recorded as current.
